prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for everyone — the right choice depends on your exact location in Miami, roof type, budget and whether you need hurricane-rated (Miami-Dade/Florida Building Code) materials and installation. I can, however, give you the practical steps to find the best contractor for a hurricane-rated roof replacement plus the exact questions and verification checks to use when vetting companies. If you tell me your Miami zip code I can give 3–5 local contractors with strong reputations to contact.

What to require from any Miami contractor for hurricane-rated replacement
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control approval (NOA) for the exact product and system the contractor will install. Ask for the NOA number and verify it on the Miami‑Dade Product Control site.  
- Wind‑uplift rating and installation method that meets the Florida Building Code for your zone (nailing/fastener pattern, adhesives, flashings).  
- Manufacturer certification (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred) — this affects warranty backstops.  
- Proof of current Florida contractor’s license and license number (verify at Florida DBPR).  
- Proof of general liability and workers’ compensation insurance (get policy numbers and carrier info).  
- Permitting and inspection: contractor must pull permits with the county/city and schedule required inspections.  
- Written, itemized contract: scope, materials (manufacturer/model/color), fastener schedule, underlayment, ventilation, drip edge, flashing details, start/completion dates, payment schedule, cleanup and lien release.  
- Warranties: manufacturer product warranty plus installer workmanship warranty (duration and what it covers). Confirm whether the installer’s warranty is transferable.  

Questions to ask every contractor
- “Do you have the Miami‑Dade NOA for the exact shingle/tile/metal system you plan to use? What is the NOA number?”  
- “Are you a certified installer with the manufacturer? Can you provide the certification?”  
- “Can you provide three recent local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated jobs?”  
- “Will you pull permits and schedule inspections? Who will be the point of contact?”  
- “What is your payment schedule and do you provide a written lien waiver at final payment?”  
- “Are you familiar with wind‑uplift requirements for my neighborhood (tell them your zip)?”  

Hurricane‑rated roofing options to consider
- Class 4 impact‑resistant shingles (UL 2218) with approved wind‑uplift attachments.  
- Concrete or clay tiles installed per NOA and with proper secondary water barrier and attachment.  
- Standing seam metal roofs or thru‑fastened systems that meet NOA/high wind ratings.  
- Engineered multi‑layer systems (underlayment + straps + rated flashings) for higher uplift resistance.

Red flags to avoid
- No local references, only out‑of‑state presence or “storm‑chasing” behavior.  
- Refusal to pull permits or pressure to pay large upfront amounts (more than a small deposit).  
- Lack of proof of insurance, missing license, or inability to provide NOA/manufacturer certification.  
- Extremely low bid that’s much lower than others with vague scope language.

Extra tips
- Get at least 3 written bids that are comparable in scope.  
- Ask about ventilation and interior moisture control — replacing the roof without addressing ventilation can shorten life expectancy.  
- Consider getting a structural engineer review if your roof framing is older or you plan to change roof material/weight (tile vs shingle).  
- Beware of Assignment-of-Benefits (AOB) pitfalls with insurance claims — know the contract terms before signing.

If you want, give me your Miami zip code (or cross‑street/neighborhood) and I’ll produce 3–5 well‑reviewed local roofing contractors to contact and a customizable checklist you can print for contractor interviews.
